job: 281 S Jefferson Ave — two decks + two lean-to covers (CEMCO steel, TimberTech Vintage Weathered Teak)
notes: OWNER 16 Oct: replace (2) lean-to roof covers and two decks. Main deck 12'x12', one set of stairs (the box step goes). Walkway 3'8" x 14'8", ~15" above grade on average, 9" at the lowest. Diamond Piers, CEMCO steel frame, TimberTech Advanced PVC Landmark American Walnut, no butt joints, divider boards, single picture frame. 6x6 posts, James Hardie soffit / rakes / fascia on the decks and the covers. No electrical. Keep the roll-down blinds. Main cover: bottom 88" above the deck at the house dropping to just under 80" at the posts — raise 3". Standing seam on both covers, black. DRAWING: house along the bottom; walkway on the left (14'8" x 44"), main deck on the right (12' x 12'); small cover posts 64" apart, 93" off the ground / 88" off the deck. SITE (Boulder County GIS): parcel 157517119033, Lot 33 Blk 10 Dutch Creek, 4,678 SF, Dutch Creek PUD (RL). Rear wall faces WNW (299.5 deg). OWNER 16 Oct (pricing): posts Douglas fir, no extra beam set, no steel up-charge, both covers' labor $4,000 total incl. roofing, decking $5.50/LF, roll-down blinds existing (no work). OWNER 16 Oct: the stair leaves the main deck's left side toward the walkway (into the yard in front of the walkway), not the front. No landing pad — the stair lands on grade. Diamond Piers $150 each (material). Total labor $7,750 (covers $4,000 of it). Margin 33.33% (owner-set, under the 40% floor). Cover framing wood: 2x8 rafters, (2)2x8 beams (2x8 ledger to match), 6x6 Douglas fir posts. Deck frame: CEMCO 600S162-54 C-joists, 600T track, all G90 (6" deep). Main cover: (2) posts across the front, not (3) — the deck beam keeps its middle pier on a steel stub. Main cover beam upgraded to a 4x10 Douglas fir (11' span between the two posts). SOLD at $36,300 (check / ACH) — margin is what that price carries. Deck posts: 6x6 Douglas fir rough on the deck-only piers (not steel stubs); every 6x6 is rough Douglas fir. OWNER 19 Oct (re-opened): field measurements — walkway 177" x 44", main deck 155" x 143" (overall 27'-8"); main cover 144" wall to drip, clear 96" at the house / 84" at the front posts; walkway cover 56" wall to drip, clear 89" at the house / 82" at the posts. Decking changed to TimberTech Vintage Weathered Teak (picture frame + dividers in Weathered Teak).

ahj_flags: Dutch Creek PUD (approved 12/15/1981, underlying R-L): the PUD final plan governs setbacks and coverage (LMC 17.28.230) and was not retrievable online. Plain R-L would need 25' rear — the existing house itself sits ~24' from the rear line, and the new main cover's roof edge ~11'-10". Confirm the PUD setbacks with Planning (303-335-4592, Planning@louisvilleco.gov) before submitting; a variance or PUD amendment is outside this scope
decks 30" or less above grade are not held to the principal-structure setbacks (Louisville deck handout); both decks are ~15"

lot coverage: covered decks count to the support posts. Lot 4,678 SF; house + garage 1,320 SF (assessor). The 2024 aerial puts the existing main cover's roof edge ~11'-4" off the wall; the new cover (posts at 11'-9", 1' overhang) reaches ~12'-9" — about +17 SF of coverage (31.3% to 31.6%; R-L max 30%, the PUD governs). If Planning holds coverage to the existing, set the new posts on the existing post line (field-measure) and let the deck run past the cover
work within 3' of a setback may need an Improvement Location Certificate (ILC) — budget a surveyor if Planning asks

Louisville amends IRC R507.1: decks supported from the house are engineered unless 30" or less above grade — the decks are under 30", but the covers (IBC App. I patio covers) and the steel frame need the stamped set; the handout asks for every sheet scaled and stamped

Louisville submittal: decking spec sheet showing ASTM E84 Class A (flame spread 25 or less) — confirm the TimberTech Vintage (Advanced PVC) data sheet lists Class A before submittal (the decking changed from Landmark)
Louisville deck handout / Fire Hardening Code
under-deck ground: gravel over 6-mil poly (or concrete) where the deck is 6' or less above grade — included under both decks

design criteria (Louisville 2024 codes): 145 mph Vult, Exposure C, SDC B (SDS 0.17), frost 36", elev. 5,337', CZ 5B; snow per the ASCE hazard tool (city's Marshall Fire sheet: 30 psf non-reducible; Boulder County layer shows 40 psf) — engineer to confirm the site value
811 locate before the piers; flood zone X (minimal)

Diamond Piers under the cover posts: the city's patio-cover guide asks for footings below the 36" frost line and 8" min. piers — submit the Diamond Pier evaluation report as the frost-protected alternate and get it accepted at plan review
